expectations.text: Rejects one refresh rate for the whole dashboard and calls it a defect.

expectations.text: States the four cadence bands carry no efficiency ranking and that all four get built.

expectations.text: Requires every tile to carry a value plus a delta against a stated prior period.

expectations.text: Puts net program contribution, cost of sale, new-to-file and top-partner share on the executive view.

expectations.text: Puts reversal rate, pending versus approved, single-partner share and conversion rate on the operator view.
expectations.evidence: OPERATOR tab: "CLICK-CONV % (vs 30d) | REVERSAL % (vs band) | PENDING vs APPROVED $ | 1-PARTNER SHARE"

expectations.text: Rejects one refresh rate for the whole dashboard and calls it a defect.
expectations.evidence: 'Refresh cadence — show it, don't fake it'... 'an unlabeled staleness gap is what triggers "why don't the numbers match" arguments,' with differentiated cadences per tile type.

expectations.text: Specifies four cadence bands: continuous or daily operational, weekly acquisition, monthly performance, and quarterly portfolio.
expectations.evidence: Only near-real-time (2-5 min), 15-30 min, and a weekly fraud tool are specified — no monthly or quarterly bands appear.

expectations.text: Assigns each band its own metrics and its own named review ritual stating who looks, in which meeting, deciding what.
expectations.evidence: No four cadence bands exist, and no named review meetings are described beyond 'managers only' for the fraud tool.

expectations.text: States the four cadence bands carry no efficiency ranking and that all four get built.
expectations.evidence: No such four-band structure or ranking statement exists.

expectations.text: Splits the dashboard into an executive view and an operator view.
expectations.evidence: 'One screen can serve both if the top layer is aggregate and every tile drills into affiliate-level detail on click — don't build four dashboards.'

expectations.text: States the two views differ in which metrics they carry, not only in level of detail.
expectations.evidence: Explicitly the opposite design: 'Same tiles for everyone' with drill-down, not different metric sets per role.

expectations.text: Places fraud and compliance signals on the operator view rather than in a separate tool.
expectations.evidence: 'The separate weekly fraud tool is the right call too — fraud review needs a queue/workflow, not a tile,' explicitly keeping it separate.

expectations.text: Gives the reason that daily decision-makers need performance and compliance signals at once.
expectations.evidence: Fraud is deliberately kept off the daily dashboard and run weekly instead.

expectations.text: Uses the layout convention KPI tiles, then trend or composition charts, then leaderboard or detail table, then alert strip.
expectations.evidence: Rows are 'Program pulse,' 'Revenue detail,' 'Operational queue' — no dedicated alert strip is included in the layout.

expectations.text: Requires every tile to carry a value plus a delta against a stated prior period.
expectations.evidence: Tiles like 'EPC (30d)' and 'Conversion rate (30d)' carry no stated delta against a prior period, only some tiles (e.g. '7d trend arrow') do.

expectations.text: Puts net program contribution, cost of sale, new-to-file and top-partner share on the executive view.
expectations.evidence: None of net program contribution, cost of sale, or new-to-file appear anywhere in the dashboard design.

expectations.text: Puts reversal rate, pending versus approved, single-partner share and conversion rate on the operator view.
expectations.evidence: Pending vs approved and conversion rate appear (e.g. 'Orders pending validation', 'Conversion rate (30d)'), but no explicit 'reversal rate' metric or 'single-partner share' percentage tile is built.
